Asturian

[edit]

Verb

Catalan

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [ˈmi.ɾə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [ˈmi.ɾa]
  • Rhymes: -iɾa

Etymology 1

[edit]

Deverbal from mirar.

Noun

[edit]

mira f (plural mires)

  1. look, glance
  2. intention, aim
  3. (weaponry) sight, scope
    Synonym: punt de mira

Etymology 2

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

mira

  1. inflection of mirar:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative
Usage notes
[edit]
  • The imperative form mira can reduce to mi in colloquial speech when one or more clitic pronouns are attached to the end of the verb. (Can we verify(+) this sense, particularly "Eh? in which dialect of Catalan would be that?)"?)

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Spanish mirar (“to look”).

Verb

[edit]

mirá

  1. to look; to look; to glance

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈmi.ra/
  • Rhymes: -ira
  • Hyphenation: mì‧ra

Etymology 1

[edit]

From mirare.

Noun

[edit]

mira f (plural mire)

  1. aim
  2. sight
    Synonym: mirino
  3. (figurative) aim, goal, purpose, design, objective, purport
    Synonyms: scopo, obiettivo, intenzione
  4. (surveying) stadia, level staff
Related terms
[edit]
  • mirare
  • mirino
  • prendere la mira
  • prendere di mira

Etymology 2

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Verb

[edit]

mira

  1. inflection of mirare:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative
    • Mira, o Norma, a' tuoi ginocchi
      Questi cari pargoletti.
      Ah! pietà di lor ti tocchi
      Se non hai di te pietà.
      Look, o Norma, at your knees
      These darling children.
      Ah! May pity for them touch you
      If you have no pity for yourself.
      (Felice Romani, libretto to Vincenzo Bellini's, Norma, Act 2, Scene 3.)

Anagrams

[edit]
  • armi, mari, rami, rima

Ladin

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

mira f (plural mires)

  1. goal, aim, end

[edit]

Adjective

mīra

    1. nominative/vocative/ablative feminine singular
    2. nominative/accusative/vocative neuter plural

References

  • (mìra): IPA(key): [ˈmʲɪ.r̺ɐ]

Noun

mirà f stress pattern 2

  2. instrumental singular of mira

Maltese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Italian mira or its Sicilian equivalent.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈmiːra/
  • Rhymes: -iːra

Noun

[edit]

mira f (plural miri)

  1. target; aim (e.g. for shooting)
  2. aim; goal; purpose
    Synonym: għan
    Ma lħaqniex il-miri tagħna. ― We didn’t reach our goals.

Portuguese

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈmi.ɾɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈmi.ɾɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈmi.ɾa/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈmi.ɾɐ/

  • Audio (Portugal):(file)
  • Audio (Portugal (Porto)):(file)
  • Rhymes: -iɾɐ
  • Homophone: Mira

Etymology 1

[edit]

Deverbal from mirar.

Noun

[edit]

mira f (plural miras)

  1. sight (device through which the person aiming looks at the intended target)
  2. marksmanship (ability to shoot accurately at a target)
    Synonym: pontaria
  3. aim (ability of someone to aim straight)
    Você tem uma mira excelente. ― You have excellent aim.

Etymology 2

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Verb

[edit]

mira

  1. inflection of mirar:
    1. third-person singular present indicative
    2. second-person singular imperative

Romanian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin mīrārī.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • Audio:(file)

Verb

[edit]

a mira (third-person singular present miră, past participle mirat, third-person subjunctive mire) 1st conjugation

  1. (reflexive) to wonder
  2. (reflexive) to be astounded, amazed, surprised
  3. (transitive) to astound, amaze
  4. (regional, Transylvania) to see to

Sora

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈmiraː/

Verb

[edit]

mira

  1. to be frightened, scared.
    Anurkidan asan tanglyneanji mirateji.
    Owing to the scent of the tiger, the oxen is frightened.

Tagalog

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Tagalog) IPA(key): /ˈmiɾa/ [ˈmiː.ɾɐ]
  • Rhymes: -iɾa
  • Syllabification: mi‧ra

Adjective

[edit]

mira (Baybayin spelling ᜋᜒᜇ) (Rizal, colloquial)

  1. clipping of primera (“too; very”)
    Mirang ganda ng kapatid niya.
    Her sibling is very beautiful.
    (literally, “Firstness in beauty of her sibling.”)
